prompt: Our crawler has a `getRobotsRules(host)` helper that every crawl worker calls before hitting a URL on that host. It's backed by a TTL cache (`robotsCache`) keyed by host, so the raw robots.txt body should only be fetched once per TTL window per host. Ops is reporting that for a specific subset of hosts, the crawler still fires a fresh robots.txt GET on every single request — never once reading from the cache — which is wasting bandwidth and risking IP bans. The one thing all the affected hosts have in common is that their robots.txt file is empty (which just means "allow all"). Walk through the code below, find exactly why the cache never registers a hit for these hosts, and tell me how you'd fix it and prove the fix works with a test.
